hypotheses.statement: EDF field structure can organize repository-authored failure and success narratives into a common diagnostic representation.
hypotheses.boundary: Repository-authored historical and teaching cases under a shared research process. This does not establish explanatory validity or external generalization.

hypotheses.statement: System Context improves semantic scope agreement beyond the effect of adding matched headings.
hypotheses.boundary: No randomized System Context ablation or matched-heading control has been completed.

hypotheses.statement: Validation Protocol v1.1 improves cross-executor reproducibility.
hypotheses.boundary: No controlled v1.0 versus v1.1 comparison and no independent replication.

hypotheses.statement: EDF improves control-point quality relative to natural analysis.
hypotheses.boundary: Authored cases often surface system-level controls (internal demonstration). In two blinded, deterministically scored benchmarks, EDF did not improve action accuracy over a general prompt (OD1), and removing the Control Points and Ranking steps was practically equivalent to full EDF (OD2, +0.54 [-0.82, 1.97]). Bounded to Claude analyzers on synthetic recognition-format cases; human analysts and real intervention outcomes are untested.

hypotheses.statement: EDF produces materially comparable semantic diagnoses under independent executor conditions.
hypotheses.boundary: No completed independent human or multi-model reproducibility study.

hypotheses.statement: EDF updates origins, confidence, and control points proportionally as evidence changes.
hypotheses.boundary: The longitudinal architecture exists, but LRC-001 has not produced completed controlled runs.

hypotheses.statement: Origin Network and Propagation are usefully distinct diagnostic constructs.
hypotheses.boundary: One direct ablation and repeated authored usage. Independent replication is absent.

hypotheses.statement: EDF adds semantic value beyond a matched neutral structured prompt.
hypotheses.boundary: Two preregistered tests compared EDF with a matched neutral structured prompt. EX-EDF-001 (two families, six cases) found +0.56 [0.00, 1.39] against a frozen +5 margin; OD1 (Claude, 12 cases) found +2.8 [0.8, 5.3], below margin, driven by the neutral protocol underperforming a general prompt rather than EDF exceeding it. Neither met the promotion rule. OD2 had no neutral arm, but its component ablations were practically equivalent to the full specification. Ceiling effects limit all three; harder, open-generation, cross-provider and human tests remain.

hypotheses.statement: Recurring diagnostic topologies generalize across unseen systems.
hypotheses.boundary: Patterns were derived from selected cases and have not been coded on a held-out set.

hypotheses.statement: EDF-0 is fast and learnable enough for routine use.
hypotheses.boundary: No time-on-task, learning-curve or human usability evidence exists. For Claude analyzers, OD1 found EDF-0 -2.1 [-3.9, -0.5] versus full EDF v0.3, so non-inferiority was inconclusive. Model performance is not evidence of human speed or learnability.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit EDF negative-knowledge semantics reduce unsupported certainty and improve preservation of unresolved alternatives under incomplete evidence.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit EDF control-point semantics improve selection of upstream mechanism-changing actions over symptom-focused actions.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit EDF propagation semantics improve classification of causal direction, mediation, and downstream effects in multi-stage systems.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit EDF evidence-update semantics improve proportional revision of hypotheses as evidence changes while preserving unresolved alternatives and prior-state distinctions.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit EDF interaction semantics improve identification of joint causal conditions when neither factor alone is sufficient.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit separation of causal mechanisms from detection and protective controls reduces harmful recommendations to disable controls that merely surface or contain failures.
hypotheses.boundary: Preregistered for EX-EDF-2026-A003. No analyzer run has occurred; this is a pending construct-specific hypothesis.

hypotheses.statement: Applying EDF v0.3 as a reasoning procedure improves language-model diagnostic outcomes over a general-purpose prompt or an established diagnostic method.
hypotheses.boundary: Three preregistered benchmarks found no material advantage, and OD2 established practical equivalence (CI within +/-3 points) against a general prompt, Kepner-Tregoe and KT + ACH on Claude Sonnet 5.5; on Haiku 5.5 EDF underperformed Kepner-Tregoe. Increasing reasoning effort improved results more, at lower cost. Bounded to Claude-family analyzers (plus GPT-5.6 Sol in EX-EDF-001), synthetic cases and recognition-format scoring near ceiling. It does not address EDF as a format for human analysts, reviewers or communication.
